ranking.note: Raised to P1: a responsibly-disclosed flaw letting release verification pass on revoked/expired keys is a release-integrity/security defect, the category's top concern, on par with #35765.
Raised to P1: the Guix codesign environment currently fails to build, which blocks the release signing process this cycle.
Raised to P2 to match #36042/#36036: same class of toolchain-baseline transition, and it is the macOS half of the Clang 19 baseline that #36036 also contains.
Raised to P2 for consistency with #36042: identical consequence (compiler baseline bump unblocking CTAD and the C++23 move).
Placed below the concrete baseline bumps it depends on (#36042/#36036/#36287), which is why it sits six positions lower than its own score.
Raised to P2: removes the Boost.Test dependency and its Guix/vcpkg/depends workarounds, a long-standing repo objective (RFC #34666, #8670) and a recurring build burden.
CI hermeticity is valuable but speculative compared with the concrete build/platform breakages placed above it.
Pure internal library restructuring with no stated breakage fixed; ranks below the P3s that fix concrete build or platform failures.
Moved up: -Wunused is cited as catching real omissions (#36137), more than the other warning-flag PRs.
Binary-size trimming is a modest optimization; grouped with #36193 below the correctness- and CI-oriented P3s.
Author confirms no CI failure has actually been observed, and #36147 may replace the setup entirely.
Convenience packaging feature with no breakage behind it; sits below P3s that fix or prevent build failures.
Lowered to P4: removing discarded linter output for 14 subtree files is the same order of marginality as #36485 and the other hygiene PRs.

inconsistencies: #36036 (Clang 19) already bumps Xcode CLT to 26.3, which is the entirety of #36287; they overlap and one supersedes the other. Review #36287 first as the smaller, self-contained decision, or fold it into #36036.

Toolchain chain: #36042 (GCC 13), #36036 (Clang 19) and #36287 (Xcode CLT) are the prerequisites for #36033 (C++23 RFC, tracking #34979). The baselines must be settled before the C++23 RFC can be judged.
#28690 adds new dependency rules to check-deps.sh while #35167 rewrites check-deps.sh in Python; they will conflict. Decide the Python rewrite (#35167) first or rebase #28690 onto it.

Multiprocess build cluster: #32387 (Windows IPC) is the enabling platform work and should be reviewed before #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect), which depends on the same #10102 track; #35454 and #36060 are small build-side fixes in the same area and can follow.
BSD CI overlap: #36147 replaces the cross-compiled BSD jobs with native VM jobs, which would obsolete the SDK-download caching #35722 improves. Settle #36147's scope first.

Native-binary CI overlap: #36082 (Guix builds plus tests on packaged artifacts) covers some of what #35774 (cross-built macOS arm64 testing) does; confirm they are not duplicating the macOS test path before merging both.
result.notes: The three P1s are the only PRs in the list with direct release-integrity consequences (wrong sources compiled, verification accepting revoked keys, broken codesign environment); everything else is platform support, CI coverage, toolchain transitions, or hygiene, which is why the P2 band is dominated by the Windows/macOS/Guix platform and baseline work. The long P3 tail is mostly interchangeable in value; ordering there reflects whether a concrete failure is being fixed versus a developer-facing improvement.
